subject: How can one get the name of a random slope covariate from an inla object?

messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: How can one get the name of a random slope covariate from an inla object?
parts:
if one fits a model of the form

my_formula ~ age + f(edu, model = "iid2d", n = 10)
                 + f(edu1, age, copy = "edu")

res = inlay(my_formula,data = my_data)

is there a way to extract the name of the random slope covariate (here age) from the resulting inla object (res).

Thanks in advance, Guido

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How can one get the name of a random slope covariate from an inla object?
parts:
thanks,

I think I also found a way to do it via the formula object:

assuming "f" is the formula object:

re = grep(".f\\(",
          strsplit(as.character(f)[[3]],"\\+")[[1]],
          value = T)
re =
sapply(re,function(x) {
  tmp = gsub("^ f\\(|\\) $","",x)
  o1 = sub("[0-9]","",strsplit(tmp,",")[[1]][1])
  o2 = trimws(strsplit(tmp,",")[[1]][2])
 
  return(c(group = o1,
           weight = ifelse(grepl("model",o2),
                           "1",
                           o2)))
})


returns for each random effect the grouping variable and the weight-variable (or the intercept)
